title: LIO-DPC: Accurate and Fast LiDAR-Inertial Odometry with Dynamic Pose Chain
problem: LiDAR-inertial odometry must balance speed and accuracy: filter-based methods are fast but suffer from cumulative errors; graph-based methods reduce errors but are computationally expensive, making real-time operation challenging.
motivation: Robotics, autonomous driving, and drone applications require precise, low-latency motion estimation; current methods force a speed-accuracy tradeoff unsuitable for real-time deployment.
method: LIO-DPC combines filter-based and graph-based approaches using a dynamic pose chain. A fast filter generates initial poses, then computationally efficient local graph optimization refines relative poses on local pose chains. Loop sparsification selects representative loops (temporally and spatially proximate) to reduce graph complexity while minimizing loop errors.
key_novelty: Dynamic pose chain optimization that bridges filter-based speed and graph-based accuracy by applying local graph optimization to selected pose chains while using sparsified loops to reduce computational burden.
contributions: Achieves real-time performance with graph-based accuracy
Loop sparsification strategy for computational efficiency
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; specific accuracy metrics and computational overhead comparisons not provided.
primary_theme: Hybrid filter-graph LiDAR odometry for real-time accuracy
